explanation.en:
時 (とき) means “when.” It connects a time or action with another action. You can use it with verbs and adjectives to say “when I do…,” “when it is…,” or “when I did….”

Key points:
• Verb (dictionary) + 時 = when you do
• Verb (past) + 時 = when you did
• Noun + の + 時 = when (noun)
• Adjective + 時 = when it is/was

Example: “日本に行く時、写真を撮ります” means “When I go to Japan, I take photos.” “暇な時、映画を見ます” means “When I am free, I watch movies.”

Use dictionary form for general or future situations, and past form for past situations. For nouns, add の before 時.

This pattern is very common and helps you talk about situations and timing in a natural way.

Practice by describing daily routines: 朝起きる時、コーヒーを飲みます. 友だちに会った時、うれしかったです.

examples.japanese: 日本に行く時、写真を撮ります。
examples.romaji: Nihon ni iku toki, shashin o torimasu.
examples.english: When I go to Japan, I take photos.

examples.japanese: 家に帰った時、シャワーを浴びます。
examples.romaji: Ie ni kaetta toki, shawaa o abimasu.
examples.english: When I got home, I take a shower.

examples.romaji: Hima na toki, eiga o mimasu.
examples.english: When I am free, I watch movies.

examples.romaji: Ame no toki, ie ni imasu.
examples.english: When it rains, I stay home.
